Title: A graph-based unsupervised log anomaly detection based on the magnetic Laplacian

Title: DRLLog: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Log Anomaly Detection
Source Title: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

Title: Anomaly Detection in Smart IoT Systems Based on Contextual Semantics of Behavior Graphs

Title: E-Log: Fine-Grained Elastic Log-Based Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis for Databases

Title: KDLog: a selective knowledge distillation approach for sequential log anomaly detection

Title: System Log Anomaly Detection With Noise-Contrastive Learning and Pattern Feature
Source Title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
Interpretability: STrees (LightGBM-based Feature Representation Decision Trees outputting leaf indices + Extremely Randomized Trees classifier) trained with Noise-Contrastive Learning (NCL) binary cross-entropy loss over fusion features

Title: LogLLM: Log-based Anomaly Detection Using Large Language Models
Interpretability: Heterogeneous LLM collaboration combining a Transformer encoder-based LLM (BERT-base), a linear representation-alignment projector, and a Transformer decoder-based LLM (Llama-3-8B, also evaluated with Qwen3-8B, GLM-4-9B, and MPT-7B) fine-tuned via QLoRA and a progressive three-stage training strategy
Preprocessing: Parser-free; dataset-independent regular expressions replacing runtime variables (booleans, numbers, dates, IPs/MACs, file paths, hex/email/host IDs, alphanumeric tokens) with <*>, session-window (HDFS) or sliding-window (BGL, Liberty, Thunderbird; window/step size 100) grouping, and Minority Class Oversampling ($\beta = 30\%$)
Notes: Compresses each log message into a single vector via the encoder LLM to preserve message boundaries and prevent decoder OOM errors; progressive 3-stage SFT (1: decoder response-format adaptation on 1,000 samples, 2: embedder/projector alignment, 3: joint fine-tuning); achieves 0.959 average $F_1$ across all four datasets (0.997 HDFS, 0.916 BGL, 0.958 Liberty, 0.966 Thunderbird), outperforming NeuralLog by 6.6%; online inference latency (0.079–0.249 s/sample) remains well below sample-generation intervals

Title: LogCALM: a log-based causal discovery and semantic modeling approach for network fault diagnosis
Interpretability: Causal graphs (PC algorithm + MixedLiNGAM + Louvain) producing human-readable root-cause-to-symptom Log Correlation Groups (LCGs), paired with a domain-pretrained BERT (mean pooling) + single-layer FC classifier that rejects low-confidence samples ($\delta = 0.5$) as "unknown"
Preprocessing: Log parsing (Drain), severity/frequency filtering, device and 1-hour window partitioning, 60-second frequency time-series construction, causal LCG extraction (PC with $G^2$ test, MixedLiNGAM with BIC scoring and $\vert{}b_{i,j}\vert{} < 0.7$ pruning, Louvain community detection), risk-level filtering ($\text{risk} > 3$), and BERT vocabulary extension with domain abbreviations plus GPT-4-refined device-manual descriptions
Notes: Decouples fault diagnosis into training-free causal LCG extraction (83% Aggregation Quality) and dual-task pre-trained BERT classification (Log Description Alignment contrastive learning + LCG-enhanced MLM); evaluated on 51.69M+ telecom backbone syslog entries, outperforming BERT, BigLog, KnowLog, and LUK ($J_{\text{sample}}$ 0.963 / 0.958, $J_{\text{macro}}$ 0.802 / 0.770); supports concept-drift detection via "unknown" rejection and human-in-the-loop retraining without catastrophic forgetting

Title: MTG-GAN: A Masked Temporal Graph Generative Adversarial Network for Cross-Domain System Log Anomaly Detection
Source Title: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
Interpretability: MTG-GAN: Graph Contrastive Learning (InfoNCE) pre-trained GCN + Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) + adaptive Gumbel-Softmax masked WGAN-GP; dual-component anomaly score combining local discriminator score ($S_w$) and global Laplacian eigenvalue divergence ($\vert{}\vert{}\delta\lambda\vert{}\vert{}_2$) to distinguish localized event anomalies from global structural shifts, plus feature perturbation contrastive loss
Preprocessing: Log parsing (Drain), window partitioning (session windows for HDFS; sliding/fixed time windows for BGL, OpenStack, and Thunderbird; 60s sliding windows with 10s stride for SWaT/WADI), and incremental multi-order temporal event graph construction into adjacency and feature matrix sequences
Notes: Targets both conventional and unsupervised cross-domain anomaly detection (BGL↔TB, BGL→SWaT/WADI, SWaT↔WADI); achieves 96.31% F1 on BGL and Thunderbird, 96.50% on OpenStack, and strong transfer F1 (0.951 BGL→TB, 0.892 TB→BGL); lightweight inference (200 MB VRAM, 12.5% GPU) with gradual long-term drift decay (~3.8% F1 drop on BGL)

Title: DUAL: A Federated Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Framework for Collaborative Business Processes
Interpretability: DUAL: client local encoders (embedding layers) with Gaussian differential privacy noise, a third-party server autoencoder + event-execution decoder ($\mathcal{D}_s$), and client local linear decoders; computes attribute- and trace-level anomaly scores using reconstruction error plus an event execution error checking whether the expected executing client matches the observed executor
Preprocessing: Client-side embedding of local sub-trace attributes, $(\epsilon, \delta)$-Differential Privacy Gaussian noise injection ($\epsilon=4, \delta=10^{-5}$), and optional Order-Revealing Encryption (ORE) of globally synchronized timestamps for chronological server-side aggregation via shared trace IDs
Notes: Addresses privacy-preserving anomaly detection in collaborative processes without sharing raw sub-traces; introduces event execution errors to resolve the global-local discrepancy; matches or slightly exceeds centralized training AP on real-life logs (+0.014 trace-level, +0.061 attribute-level) while outperforming Local and SplitAD; statistically invariant to client count ($K=1\dots9$) and model-agnostic across AE, VAE, LAE, BINet, and GRASPED

Preprocessing: Log parsing (public parsed templates for HDFS/BGL and Spell for Thunderbird; also tested with Drain and Spell for parsing-noise robustness), session-window (HDFS) or sliding-window (BGL, Thunderbird; window size 20, step 10) grouping, 300-D semantic vector representation, and ESR under-sampling ($\le 10\%$) merging prior representative samples into current task training sets
Notes: Mitigates catastrophic forgetting and intransigence during software log evolution without full retraining; outperforms SOTA LAD baselines (DeepLog, LogAnomaly, LogRobust, LightLog, PLELog) and IL baselines (EWC, MAS, SI, SCP, DCE, SOYO); maintains strong robustness under 5%–10% label noise and Drain/Spell parsing errors; TSLANet and LSTM yield the highest backbone adaptability, while authors note ESR is currently limited to discrete sequences rather than log graphs
